findings.quoted_text: All intellectual property rights in each Deliverable transfer to Client upon delivery.
Client may terminate this Agreement at any time, without notice and without further payment.
Invoices are payable Net 30. An invoice that remains unpaid after the due date may accrue interest at 1.0% per month to the extent permitted by applicable law.
All intellectual property rights in each Deliverable transfer to Client upon delivery.
findings.explanation: The contractor loses ownership of the work as soon as it is handed over, even if the client later delays or refuses payment. This leaves the contractor without leverage to enforce payment and without protection of their IP until they are paid.
findings.suggested_change: Modify the clause to transfer IP only upon receipt of full payment for the corresponding Deliverable, e.g., "All intellectual property rights in each Deliverable transfer to Client upon full payment of the invoice related to that Deliverable."

findings.quoted_text: Client may terminate this Agreement at any time, without notice and without further payment.
findings.explanation: The client can end the contract abruptly, leaving the contractor with unrecovered labor, sunk costs, and no compensation for work already performed. This creates financial uncertainty and undermines the contractor’s ability to plan resources.
findings.suggested_change: Replace with a mutual termination clause that requires written notice (e.g., 15 days) and payment of all undisputed fees for work performed up to termination, e.g., "Either party may terminate for material breach after 15 days' cure period, or by mutual written agreement. Upon termination, the client shall pay all undisputed fees for Services performed up to the termination date."

findings.quoted_text: Invoices are payable Net 30. An invoice that remains unpaid after the due date may accrue interest at 1.0% per month to the extent permitted by applicable law.
findings.explanation: A 30‑day payment window combined with a modest 1% monthly interest may delay cash flow, especially if the client disputes invoices. The contractor bears the risk of late payments without strong incentives for prompt settlement.
findings.suggested_change: Shorten the payment period and increase the late‑payment penalty, e.g., "Invoices are payable Net 15. Unpaid invoices will accrue interest at 2% per month (or the maximum lawful rate) from the due date until paid."

findings.explanation: The client has 30 days after invoice to pay and only a 1% annual interest on late amounts, which may not provide enough incentive for timely payment and could leave you waiting for cash flow, especially if the client delays multiple milestones.
findings.suggested_change: Negotiate a shorter net period (e.g., Net 14) and a higher late‑payment rate (e.g., 1.5‑2% per month) or include a clause that allows you to suspend work after a 15‑day overdue period until payment is received.

findings.explanation: Only three revision cycles are explicitly allowed. If the client requests additional changes beyond these rounds, they may claim they are within the agreed scope, leading to extra unpaid work or disputes.
findings.suggested_change: Add language that any revisions beyond the three allotted rounds will be treated as a change request and billed at an agreed hourly or fixed rate, with prior written approval required.

content.subject: Proposed changes to the agreement
content.body:
Hello,

- The relevant clause transfers all intellectual property rights in each Deliverable to the Client upon delivery, which means I would lose ownership before receiving payment. I propose to modify the clause so that IP transfers only after full payment for the corresponding Deliverable, e.g., "All intellectual property rights in each Deliverable transfer to Client upon full payment of the invoice related to that Deliverable."
- The relevant clause allows the Client to terminate the agreement at any time without notice or further payment, leaving me without compensation for work already performed. I suggest replacing it with a mutual termination provision that requires written notice (e.g., 15 days) and payment of all undisputed fees for services performed up to termination.
- The relevant clause sets invoices payable Net 30 and accrues interest at 1% per month on late payments, which may affect cash flow. I recommend shortening the payment period to Net 15 and increasing the late‑payment interest to 2% per month (or the maximum lawful rate) from the due date until paid.
- The relevant clause limits revisions to three rounds, which could result in extra unpaid work. I propose adding language that any revisions beyond the three allotted rounds will be treated as a change request and billed at an agreed rate, with prior written approval required.

Thank you for reviewing these suggestions. I look forward to finalizing the agreement.
